hypotheses_validated.claim: modelfile.c parses every container written by python/hearth/format.py exactly as ContainerReader + apply_defaults does (config incl. defaults, tensor directory and bytes, expert entries, distinct-slab region size).
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Scratch cross-check (test_modelfile --dump vs ContainerReader): synth.make_tiny for qwen3_moe/olmoe/mixtral/qwen2_moe/deepseek_v3 x F32/F16/BF16/Q8/Q4 = 25/25 agree; synth.make_shaped with physical_experts=3 (aliased slabs, GQA and MLA+dense layer+shared expert) 2/2 agree. Q8/Q4 synthesis used a scratch DLL built from quant.c only (T08's api.c does not exist yet).

hypotheses_validated.claim: The reader never crashes or reads out of bounds on malformed input and rejects every structurally invalid variant with a message (INV-FMT, INV-SAFE).
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_modelfile: 200 random valid containers round-tripped field by field (load_dense 0/1), then ~5,000-9,000 variants per run (truncation at every section/entry/tensor/slab boundary +-1 and random points; preamble huge/overflowing counts and offsets; tensor and expert entry misalignment, overlap with sections/tensors/slabs, out-of-range, bad dtype/ndim/shape/name/duplicates; metadata bad types, bad UTF-8 (overlong, surrogate, >U+10FFFF), length overflows, missing required keys, inconsistent dims; random byte flips). Clean under MSVC /fsanitize=address (seeds 4-8, up to 8983 variants) and gcc 13.3 -fsanitize=address,undefined with LeakSanitizer (WSL2).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Every slab the store hands out holds the file's bytes for that (layer, expert), under concurrency, and stays intact until released.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_store hashes each slab at acquire and again (via a second acquire) right before release: 96 configurations (LRU/LFU x 1,2,3,4,8,16 readers x min/min+3/40/all slots x direct/buffered, 1-4 caller threads), ~350k random acquire/try_acquire/release/prefetch/tick/wait_any operations per run, mixed-dtype slabs (8-48 KiB) with ~15% aliased entries. 0 failures over seeds 1-5 and 21, also under MSVC ASan and gcc ASan+UBSan.

hypotheses_validated.claim: No deadlock at the minimum slot count (2*top_k + n_io + 2) with all top-k of a layer demanded at once while the previous layer's top-k is still held.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: min_slots_burst: 1/2/4/16 readers x LRU/LFU, 60 tokens x 5 MoE layers, with prefetch noise, under a 60 s no-progress watchdog.

hypotheses_validated.claim: A caller that demands more experts than there are slots (batch union) and then blocks in acquire or wait_any on a late one would deadlock if demanded-but-uncollected slabs stayed protected; dropping those holds when a blocked caller finds the store starved with nothing in flight (and waking readers at tick) removes the deadlock.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: overcommit test (80 experts into 11-26 slots; reverse-order blocking acquire; tick then busy-poll of the queue head; wait_any-only polling of the last expert). Scratch builds with each of the three fixes removed hang in exactly that phase (watchdog fires after 60 s); the real build passes.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Global LRU collapses under cyclic layer access when the cache is smaller than one token's working set; LFU keeps a substantial hit rate on Zipf-skewed routing.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_store policy check (synthetic trace): 8 MoE layers x top-4 = 32 slabs/token, 16-slot cache, Zipf(1.2) per layer, 800 tokens: LRU hit rate 0.000, LFU 0.258 (asserted: LRU < 0.05, LFU > 0.20 and > 4x LRU).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Reads are spread over mirrors and non-identical mirrors are refused.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: A mirror differing only in the last 8 bytes of one slab (invisible to the open-time spot check): over 60 forced re-reads that slab came 24-30 times from the primary and 30-36 times from the mirror. Mirrors differing in size, preamble, metadata, tensor directory, expert directory, first slab page or a mid-file slab page are rejected at open.

Final sources: store.c 65.0% (80 sampled: 37 killed, 15 detected as hangs, 28 survived), modelfile.c 80.0% (60 sampled: 45 killed, 3 timeouts, 12 survived). Every survivor reviewed: leak/destroy-only (free/hx_mutex_destroy removed; MSVC ASan has no leak checker, the gcc LSan run is clean), out-of-memory and SIZE_MAX paths, log/message-only lines, equivalent tie-breaks/sentinels/redundant guards, mirror retry rotation (needs a read that fails on only one byte-identical copy). Earlier rounds found real gaps (holds, protection order, prefetch eviction, mirror header comparison, pin tie order, alignment-only slab errors, UTF-8 overlongs, rope_inv_freq shape) which were then covered.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Fixed scratch file names in %TEMP% are fine for the C tests.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: The first store mutation run executed test_store in 4 parallel jobs that clobbered each other's container ('file not found' failures); that run's score was discarded. Scratch names now carry a per-process tag and HEARTH_MUTATION_TMP is preferred.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Holding demanded slabs until collected (or token end) is enough to prevent eviction thrash without risking deadlock.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Not for callers that demand more than fits and block on a late expert (see overcommit ledger entry); holds now also drop when a blocked caller finds the store starved.

open_questions: hx_store_acquire returns NULL after 3 failed read attempts (a slab past EOF / I/O error), contrary to the header's 'never NULL for valid ids'; try_acquire on such an expert keeps returning NULL and wait_any returns at once when nothing else is pending, so a polling engine loop would spin. Needs a contract decision (see contract_issues).

Per-layer canonical tensor shapes/dtypes (FORMAT 4.1 table) are NOT validated by modelfile.c, only rope_inv_freq; model.c (T08) must check every tensor it binds or out-of-bounds reads are possible on crafted files.
Dense-region load uses up to 4 threads of 64 MiB unbuffered reads; its throughput on a multi-GB backbone was not measured.
Benchmark peak for 2.39 MiB slabs is at 2 readers (7.0 GB/s) and drifts to ~6.0 GB/s at 4-16; whether that is the SSD or the overlapped-handle path was not investigated.
